primary_sources.source: Republic Act No. 10121, Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Sections 5-6 establish the NDRRMC and its policy and coordination functions; Section 9 assigns OCD duties including standard operating procedures for rapid assessment, coordination, information sharing, and incident command; Sections 11-12 establish local councils and LDRRMOs and assign local risk assessment, early warning, operations-center, reporting, training, and response-coordination functions. Section 12 makes the LDRRMO responsible to the local chief executive and council, not to a software vendor.

primary_sources.source: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Operations Center Standard Operating Procedures and Guidelines, 2024 Edition
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Defines report development, review, approval, publication, documentation, and incident-report classifications. Initial reports communicate first available information; progress reports update incident status, actions, and developments and are expected to be substantiated; terminal reports close an incident or phase with final impact figures. The guideline also requires source coordination, treats health-outbreak terminology as dependent on an authorized health-office declaration, and maintains PDF/Excel backups for later verification.

primary_sources.source: National Disaster Response Plan, Consequence Management for Terrorism-Related Incidents
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Identifies the Incident Command System as the Philippine on-scene disaster-response system and connects it to OCD's authority under RA 10121 Section 9(g). This supports role-, command-, and operational-period-aware reporting, while leaving actual command authority with appointed incident personnel.

primary_sources.date: manual series; editions vary by hazard
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Provides hazard-specific preparedness actions and LGU checklists for typhoons, localized weather disturbances, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruption, and other contingencies. It is evidence for configurable hazard checklists and role-linked preparedness records, not evidence that one digital workflow is legally prescribed for every hazard.

primary_sources.source: ISO 22320:2018 Security and resilience — Emergency management — Guidelines for incident management
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Provides incident-management guidance on principles, processes, organizational structures, roles and responsibilities, resource management, joint direction, and cooperation among organizations that may retain their own structures.

Defines an XML format for alerts and public warnings, including identifiers, sender, sent time, status, message type, scope, references, event category, urgency, severity, certainty, instructions, resources, and geographic areas. Alert, Update, Cancel, Ack, and Error messages have explicit reference semantics. CAP does not define a complete internal incident case record or SitRep workflow.

Published series demonstrate numbered, time-stamped SitRep versions over an incident's life. They support evaluation of numbering, as-of timestamps, supersession, and reproducible export, but do not by themselves disclose every internal verification rule.

evidence.legal_or_evidentiary_status: RA 10121 is binding Philippine law and controls institutional authority. The 2024 NDRRMOC SOPG is authoritative operational guidance for NDRRMOC reporting; applying its exact workflow to every LGU or private customer requires adoption or configuration rather than assumption. Official response plans and Operation L!STO manuals are government guidance within their stated incident or hazard scope. ISO 22320 is voluntary unless incorporated into contract, policy, procurement, or regulation. CAP 1.2 is a technical message standard, not a delegation of warning authority. The system design below is therefore an evidence-based implementation proposal: it may support authorized personnel but cannot appoint incident command, validate facts by itself, declare an outbreak or calamity, or turn a startup-generated document into an official government issuance.
evidence.evidence_limits_and_conflicts: The complete paid text of ISO 22320 was not available for clause-level inspection, so only ISO's official abstract and status are relied upon. Operation L!STO editions and checklists differ by hazard and must not be collapsed into one universal mandatory sequence. RA 10121 establishes responsibilities but does not prescribe the proposed database schema, identifiers, tenant model, or UI. The NDRRMOC SOPG governs national operations-center practice; local adoption and customer-specific approval chains must be confirmed. Reported figures can conflict because they reflect different sources, geographic units, cut-off times, and verification states. The product should preserve conflict and provenance instead of silently selecting the largest, latest, or most convenient number. CAP covers alerts and warnings; mapping an entire SitRep to CAP would lose case history, assessment evidence, actions, resource status, and internal approvals. No cited source establishes that digitization alone reduces casualties, response time, or economic loss.

chapter_one_integration.objective_revisions: User and Organization Management: implement tenant-scoped organizations, memberships, and least-privilege roles for reporter, verifier, approver, administrator, and read-only viewer, while recording who performed each governed action. Disaster Reporting: capture incident identity, hazard/event type, occurrence and observation times, reporting source, location, narrative, attachments, affected people and infrastructure, actions, needs, and confidence/verification state; accept partial initial reports without presenting unknown values as zero. Verification: provide field-level source attribution, duplicate and conflict flags, request-for-clarification, corroboration records, acceptance/rejection reasons, and an immutable decision log; human authorities remain accountable. SitRep Generation: assemble a selected cut-off snapshot into initial, progress, terminal, or customer-configured reports; show report number, as-of time, operational period, sources, unresolved conflicts, approval status, version, corrections, and superseded report reference. Catalog: maintain customer-approved hazards, report categories, geographic units, organizations, units of measure, verification statuses, and impact/action categories with versioned codes and local labels. Dashboard: summarize verified and provisional values separately, expose data freshness and coverage, permit drill-down to source reports, and avoid totals across incompatible cut-off times or units. Evaluation: measure task completion, field completeness, provenance coverage, conflict-detection precision, approval errors, report-generation time, export fidelity, usability, accessibility, tenant isolation, and recovery under defined datasets and network conditions. These are prototype submodule objectives; automated truth determination, command decisions, dispatch, forecasting, and official public warning are excluded.
chapter_one_integration.scope_inclusions: Actors include customer administrators, authorized reporters, validators/verifiers, SitRep developers, approvers, viewers, records/privacy personnel, and startup support staff with explicitly limited access. Organization levels may include barangay, city/municipality, province, region, national agency, civil-society or private partner, but each deployment must configure actual jurisdiction and escalation routes. Hazards may use customer-approved controlled vocabularies and hazard-specific fields rather than a false universal checklist. Records cover raw reports, observations, attachments, verification evidence, conflicts, actions, needs, impact figures, revisions, approvals, exports, access/audit events, and catalog versions. Workflow includes draft, submitted, triaged, under verification, verified in whole or part, rejected/returned, included in a report snapshot, approved, published/exported, corrected, superseded, terminal, archived, and disposed states. The service may generate human-readable PDF/structured exports and an optional CAP-compatible alert message only when an authorized customer workflow expressly calls for one. Customer configuration, onboarding, support, backup, restoration, export, and offboarding are in scope because the product is a startup service, not merely an internal ZCDRRMO application.
chapter_one_integration.limitations_and_delimitations: The prototype is not an emergency dispatch, 911, radio, sensor, forecasting, GIS risk-modeling, resource-tracking, case-management, damage-assessment certification, disease-surveillance, or public-warning authority system. It does not replace ICS forms, agency command structures, NDRRMC systems, DILG checklists, field validation, or statutory records processes. CAP export is limited to alert/warning semantics and requires an authorized sender, a customer CAP profile, endpoint agreement, authentication, and conformance testing; generic API or file export does not establish interoperability. Offline operation, satellite/SMS transport, automated agency integration, digital signatures with legal effect, nationwide master-data harmonization, and cross-agency identity federation are outside the student prototype unless separately implemented and tested. Deployment evidence from one office, hazard, language, device set, or prepared dataset cannot be generalized to all Philippine LGUs. Connectivity, source quality, staffing, local policy, retention schedules, and third-party services remain dependencies.

significance_causal_chains.authorized_reporters: Structured fields plus saved provenance produce more complete, traceable submissions; this may reduce re-entry and clarification effort if forms fit field practice and work on available devices. Poorly fitted required fields can delay urgent reporting, so progressive completion and usability evidence are prerequisites.
significance_causal_chains.verifiers_and_sitrep_developers: Source-linked claims, conflict queues, cut-off snapshots, and version comparison make review status visible and reports reproducible; this may reduce unnoticed copying and reconciliation effort. Benefit requires maintained catalogs, staffing, and disciplined use; automation bias remains a harm.
significance_causal_chains.incident_managers_and_decision_makers: Freshness, uncertainty, jurisdiction, and drill-down displays can improve comprehension of what is known and contested. They do not ensure better decisions; evaluation must test interpretation accuracy and decision-process fit without claiming casualty reduction.
significance_causal_chains.customer_organizations: Tenant-scoped administration, configurable workflows, export, and audit records can support consistent governance and accountability. Value depends on lawful procurement, privacy/records rules, training, service continuity, and an exit mechanism; lock-in and tenant leakage are material harms.
significance_causal_chains.communities_and_public: More traceable official information may indirectly support clearer authorized communication, but only after human approval and through official channels. Premature, privacy-invasive, or misleading publication can cause harm; the startup must not claim public authority.
significance_causal_chains.researchers_and_developers: A bounded prototype and evaluation dataset can document design trade-offs in Philippine SitRep digitization. Findings support this artifact and test setting, not nationwide effectiveness or market demand without multi-site evidence.

safe: The system is designed to preserve the source, cut-off time, verification state, and version of information used in each generated SitRep.
RA 10121 assigns DRRM authority and responsibilities to government bodies; the proposed startup supplies configurable software and support rather than assuming those powers.
The 2024 NDRRMOC SOPG distinguishes initial, progress, and terminal incident reports and expects progress information to be substantiated by documentation.
CAP may be offered as a bounded export for authorized alert workflows, but it is not a substitute for the complete SitRep record.
Dashboard indicators separate provisional from verified values and link aggregates to source records.
avoid: The platform verifies disasters automatically or guarantees accurate reports.
The startup is the official Philippine disaster-reporting or warning system.
CAP integration makes the platform interoperable with every government system.
The dashboard provides real-time data when latency and source update intervals have not been measured.
Use of the system improves response, saves lives, or reduces losses without comparative field evidence.
Compliance with RA 10121, ISO 22320, or NDRRMC procedures unless a scoped conformity assessment has been completed.

authority_and_responsibility_matrix.reporter: Creates and corrects observations within assigned organization and jurisdiction; identifies source and time; cannot mark their own claim officially verified unless local policy expressly combines roles.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.verifier: Checks claims and evidence, records field-level decisions and reasons, requests clarification, and preserves contradictory reports; does not rewrite the reporter's original record.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.approver_or_official_submitter: Selects the authoritative snapshot, accepts residual uncertainty, approves issuance/export, and determines official recipients under customer policy.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.incident_command_or_customer_authority: Defines operational period, reporting priorities, jurisdiction, terminology, and command decisions; remains outside startup control.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.customer_administrator: Manages tenant membership, role assignment, catalogs, workflow configuration, retention rules, and integrations subject to segregation of duties.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.records_and_privacy_authority: Sets lawful basis, access classification, retention/disposition, disclosure, correction, and data-subject procedures; approves sensitive-data handling.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.startup_personnel: Operate hosting, security, backup, support, incident response, and audited break-glass access under contract; cannot approve facts or publish official government reports.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.external_agency: Owns its source system and interface, authenticates exchanges, defines acceptance and error handling, and remains authoritative for its data.

system_and_governance.workflow_lineage_and_data_lifecycle: Assign an immutable tenant-scoped incident UUID plus human-readable customer incident number; each source submission receives its own identifier and preserves source organization, reporter, reported-at, observed/occurred-at, received-at, location/jurisdiction, channel, and original content hash. Store facts as claims with value, unit, category-code version, geographic scope, valid/as-of time, evidence links, confidence/verification state, and verifier decision. Link duplicates rather than deleting them. Represent conflict as an explicit relationship among claims; resolution records the selected claim, rationale, responsible person, time, and alternatives, without overwriting originals. A SitRep version is an immutable snapshot of included claim versions at a declared cut-off and operational period. Draft, reviewed, approved, issued/exported, corrected, superseded, and terminal transitions require actor/time/reason; a correction creates a new version and references the superseded one. Use customer-approved classification and retention schedules; legal holds suspend disposition. Export must carry identifiers, timestamps, units, code versions, classification, and verification state. Archive and deletion must be logged, with backup expiry aligned to disposition rather than allowing deleted records to persist indefinitely.

module_specific_requirements.User and Organization Management: Tenant boundary on every record and query; scoped organization membership; least privilege; MFA for privileged roles where feasible; role-change and break-glass audit; deactivation without destroying authored history; no startup superuser access by default.
module_specific_requirements.Disaster Reporting: Progressive form; stable incident and submission IDs; occurrence/observation/report times; jurisdiction and geocode; source channel and contact restrictions; hazard and impact catalogs; units; attachments with integrity metadata; unknown/not-applicable distinct from zero; duplicate suggestion without automatic merge.
module_specific_requirements.Verification: Field-level decisions; source-authority ranking configured by customer and treated as guidance rather than automatic truth; corroboration and contradiction links; clarification loop; reason codes plus notes; segregation-of-duties warning; original-preserving corrections.
module_specific_requirements.SitRep Generation: Initial/progress/terminal templates; explicit cut-off and operational period; report number/version; verified and provisional sections; unresolved-conflict disclosure; source notes; approval gate; reproducible PDF and structured export; correction/supersession references.
module_specific_requirements.Catalog: Versioned tenant catalogs for hazards, incident/report types, impact categories, actions, needs, administrative areas, organizations, units, states, and reason codes; effective dates; aliases and mappings; prevent deletion of used codes; keep local labels separate from interchange codes such as CAP categories.
module_specific_requirements.Dashboard: Freshness and coverage indicators; separate verified/provisional counts; compatible-unit and compatible-time aggregation only; jurisdiction filters; source drill-down; accessible tables as alternatives to charts; visible last-updated and denominator; suppression of sensitive small-cell or personal data.

system_and_governance.risk_controls_and_residual_limits: Apply tenant-scoped authorization in the data-access layer and test cross-tenant reads/writes; encrypt transport and managed storage; minimize personal and precise-location data; classify attachments; malware-scan uploads; use append-only audit events with restricted export; rate-limit and monitor privileged actions; back up and conduct restore tests; document recovery objectives; support accessible keyboard and screen-reader operation; preserve offline-safe drafts if implemented. Human approval, uncertainty display, source drill-down, and no automatic conflict suppression reduce automation bias. Residual risks include compromised customer accounts, malicious or mistaken reports, inference/re-identification from incident detail, delayed synchronization, cloud or identity-provider outage, catalog mismatch, and authorized-user misuse. Controls require evidence from authorization tests, restore exercises, accessibility checks, logging review, and incident-response drills; a checklist alone is not assurance.

evaluation_and_feasibility.metrics_comparators_and_test_conditions: Use a de-identified scenario set containing duplicates, contradictory casualty/affected-family figures, late reports, mixed units, corrections, multiple jurisdictions, partial connectivity, and sensitive attachments. Compare the prototype with the customer's current spreadsheet/document workflow using the same trained participants and tasks. Measure: report-field completeness = populated applicable required fields/applicable required fields; provenance coverage = displayed factual claims with source and as-of time/all displayed factual claims; conflict recall and precision against an expert-labeled set; unauthorized-action prevention = blocked prohibited attempts/all prohibited attempts; tenant-isolation failures across scripted cross-tenant tests; snapshot reproducibility = regenerated fields matching approved snapshot/all fields; correction traceability = sampled corrected facts retaining prior value, actor, reason, and supersession/sample; median task time and error count; System Usability Scale with sample size reported; WCAG-oriented keyboard, focus, label, contrast, and screen-reader task checks; export schema/conformance validation where a declared profile exists; backup restore success and recovery time. Report devices, browsers, network latency/outage pattern, roles, training, dataset size, and confidence intervals or raw distributions. Thresholds must be justified by stakeholder risk tolerance or baseline performance, not chosen after results.
evaluation_and_feasibility.adoption_cost_and_service_dependencies: Feasibility includes customer workflow mapping, catalog setup, data migration, account administration, verifier/approver staffing, training and exercises, privacy/records review, hosting, monitoring, backup, support coverage, incident response, periodic access review, and integration maintenance. Record one-time and recurring labor, infrastructure, messaging/storage, and support costs; do not infer willingness to pay from usability. Define service availability, support hours, recovery objectives, maintenance notices, data location, breach notification, export format, deletion timing, subcontractors, and termination assistance. Provide full tenant export plus code lists and attachments so customers can exit. Broader procurement claims require a deployable security posture, legal review, total-cost comparison, and evidence from actual customers rather than a student prototype demonstration.
evaluation_and_feasibility.generalization_and_future_evidence: The design may be evaluated for the participating office, selected roles, configured hazards, language, devices, and simulated or historical dataset only. It does not establish suitability for all barangays, geographically isolated areas, national operations, armed-conflict incidents, health outbreaks, accessibility populations, or high-volume multi-agency response. Production evidence should include multi-site pilots across LGU levels and hazard types; exercises with ICS roles and operational periods; longitudinal completeness and correction data; independent security and privacy testing; disaster-recovery exercises; accessible use with people with disabilities; offline/low-bandwidth trials; customer-specific records and approval validation; CAP profile and endpoint conformance where applicable; and governance review by competent DRRM, records, privacy, and legal authorities. Claims of operational, public-safety, economic, or market benefit require prospective comparative evidence and cannot be inferred from technical success alone.
